alternatives.argument: The local definition explicitly fixes H as real L2([0,1]), defines a measurable causal map on the countable innovation product, constructs each independent-tail replacement including full replacement at m=0, and defines delta_m and the summability condition. Its product measurability, strong measurability, and L2 integrability conventions are stated with exact local suppliers.

The local proof computes the finite lag covariance, handles zero variance in L2, clips and centers scalar projections, separates independent blocks by m discarded indices, verifies the Lindeberg condition from bounded block size, removes gaps in L2, removes clipping by a second-moment bound, and concludes by characteristic functions and Cramér-Wold. It includes singular covariance.

The local proof establishes representative-independent product kernels and their norm identity, defines the integral operator by section integration, proves its L2 bound by Cauchy-Schwarz and Fubini, identifies product kernels with rank-one operators, and factors product-kernel inner products by an absolutely integrable Fubini calculation.

The local proof constructs Bochner rank-one and product-kernel expectations, uses disjoint original/replacement coordinate sigma-algebras to center the independent truncation term, obtains trace-norm and kernel-norm lag bounds sigma*delta_(j-1), sums both series, proves normalized covariance convergence and positivity, and identifies the kernel-series integral operator with Gamma using dense rectangle kernels.

The local proof bounds the L2 distance between original and m-replaced normalized sums by delta_m^2 plus a summable-lag term and 2*sigma*(m-1)*delta_m. It uses summability only to choose a subsequence m_r with m_r*delta_(m_r)->0, transfers finite-dimensional covariances, applies the local finite-dependent CLT and characteristic-function comparison, and controls the remaining Hilbert tails using the long-run covariance lag bound, Parseval, Tonelli and bounded-uniformly-continuous tests.

The local proof uses the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem to select a finite or countable eigenbasis, sums λ_j Z_j² and uses Tonelli to show it is finite almost surely, defines the eigenseries on that full-measure set and zero on its null complement, proves Borel and strong measurability, and verifies all scalar normal laws and covariance limits. It includes finite-rank and zero covariance.
